messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — planning to create release/1.12 on Friday 09:00 PST. Need final backport asks, changelog nudges, and any must-have cherry-picks by EOD Thursday.

maya: Main checkpoints:
- version bump PR merged to main
- changelog entry in /docs/changelog.md
- backport label on PRs that need to land in 1.11
- any risky fixes require a +1 from oncall or eng leads

santiago: Copy. Which branch name are we using exactly? release/1.12 or release/v1.12?

maya: release/1.12 (we've standardized on no "v" for branch names).

drew: Quick status: version bump PR #9246 is green, waiting for lucy to confirm the changelog blurb.

lucy: I posted a short changelog note in PR #9260, can someone skim? small wording tweak might help.

jen: pinging here — #9260 looks fine to me, just a nit about the wording under "performance". +1 if maya is happy.

maya: @lucy can you update the one-line to: "Reduce average latency for small requests by ~12% via batching tweak" and I'll merge.

lucy: done and pushed. thanks.

release-bot: [automated] branch protection status: main -> green, tests: 312 passed, 2 flaky skipped.

maya: For backports: please add label backport/1.11 and put the target PR number in the PR description as: "Backport-to: release/1.11". We will only accept backports that: security/fix, data-loss, or regression severity P0/P1.

drew: Small question — does dependency bump for lib-encoder qualify? it fixed a crash on long contexts but not a regression caused by our code.

maya: If it causes customer-visible crashes on >=1.11 then yes. If it's just a perf nicety, hold to next minor. Leave a note here and I'll make the call.

drew: Filed #9275 and added backport/1.11. It fixes crash. Requesting backport.

santiago: Two process notes to keep tidy:
1) If you need a manual cherry-pick, add the label cherrypick/required and ping me. I'll coordinate the branch create+push.
2) For automated backports we run the script: 
```
./scripts/backport.sh --from PR# --to release/1.11
```
Please attach the output in the PR comment.

lucy: Thanks — copying that into our team checklist.

jen: Any time budget for non-critical cherrypicks? i have one small doc fix that would be nice to include.

maya: Non-critical doc fixes should wait for post-cut unless they affect onboarding flows. If it's <5 lines and low risk, we can squeeze it but it must be a direct commit to release/1.12 after branch creation (no hotfix dance). Add label cherrypick/docs and I'll decide during cut.

release-bot: [deploy] scheduled branch creation at Fri 09:00 PST. Will post result in this thread.

santiago: One more: please ensure anyone requesting a backport includes the following in PR body:
- reason: (security/regression/perf/other)
- impact: (customers affected, severity)
- test plan: (how to verify)

maya: Good template. If you can't fill out the test plan we may reject the backport.

drew: For the actual cut, what's our rollback plan if the branch has a big regression?

maya: Plan A: revert the merge that introduced regression on the release branch and re-cut quickly. Plan B: if multiple fixes needed, hold the branch and do a follow-up patch release. We'll have oncall & release leads on standby for 2 hours after cut.

lucy: I'll be in the channel during cut window and available for changelog fixes.

jen: I'll watch post-cut alerting and be ready to triage any customer-facing issues.

maya: Final asks:
- by EOD Thu: drop any backport labels + PR numbers here
- by Thu 23:59 PST: any changelog entries + approval from Maya or Jen
- Fri 09:00 PST: branch creation, notify QA for smoke tests

maya: thanks all — please keep messages short here so release-bot summary is easy to parse. :thumbsup:

release-bot: [automated] thread reminder posted 2 hours before cutoff.
